newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline firmer, traders eye U.S. gains for ar.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline firmer, traders eye U.S. gains for ar.

text.p: NWE gasoline trade was choppy on Thursday but prices ended generally firmer and the market's bullish undertone ahead of the spring driving season remained intact, traders said.

Trader hedge play boosted the barge market in early business before refiner selling dipped prices by around $4. Later, stronger NYMEX unleaded futures prompted talk of fresh arbitrage opportunities and prices recovered slightly, although the sharp futures' gain left trade thin.
Gasoline barges were bid up $1/$2, by one of the two trade houses that have been consistent buyers of Eurograde this week.
Early business was seen at $207 fob ARA but selling by a Scandinavian refiner saw trade down to $203 after this.
Crack spreads held around $5.50 a barrel on April with the second quarter talking $5.45.

Some traders said the chance of arbitrage to the Asia Pacific or the United States justified the physical barge market strength, but others saw the higher traded levels related to the swaps related hedging by the two trade houses.
Cargo prices were steady to firmer. Traders said there were few stems on offer as sellers watched for an opening in the arbitrage window to the U.S.
